macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks finish mixed as Dow rallies
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.02% to 52,495.88 and the S&P 500 gained 0.28% to 7,712.57, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.02% amid strong earnings and concerns about AI-related credit risks.

items.title: Global markets edge higher as earnings support sentiment
items.summary: European shares and U.S. futures moved higher as investors focused on strong corporate earnings, though rising oil prices and concerns about the sustainability of the AI trade continued to weigh on bonds and risk appetite.

items.title: SpaceX surges after strong profit and Tesla merger discussions
items.summary: SpaceX shares jumped more than 8% premarket after the company reported quarterly profit above expectations. Elon Musk said SpaceX and Tesla had formed committees to discuss a possible merger, while emphasizing that no imminent deal was assured.

items.title: Netflix falls after weaker advertising outlook
items.summary: Netflix shares dropped more than 6% premarket after the company lowered its advertising-sales guidance, raising concerns about revenue growth despite reporting third-quarter profit above Wall Street expectations.

items.title: Super Micro rallies on strong AI demand forecast
items.summary: Super Micro Computer shares rose 12% after the AI-server maker forecast quarterly revenue and profit margins above analyst estimates, signaling continued demand for AI infrastructure.

items.title: Treasury yields rise as oil returns above $110
items.summary: Brent crude climbed above $110 a barrel, contributing to pressure in global bond markets. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5.13%, while investors continued to assess inflation and the outlook for Federal Reserve policy.

items.title: Weak housing data highlights pressure from high rates
items.summary: U.S. pending home sales fell to a record low in September as average 30-year mortgage rates exceeded 7%, underscoring the economic drag from elevated borrowing costs and contributing to lower Treasury yields in earlier trading.

items.title: RBA official warns inflation outlook has worsened
items.summary: Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said the inflation outlook was materially worse and that forthcoming third-quarter inflation data were likely to confirm the deterioration.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds above $83,000 amid volatile trading
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $83,000–$83,400 after failing to sustain a move toward $87,000. Crypto derivatives liquidations reached about $286 million, with short positions accounting for most losses.[1][5]

items.title: OCC finalizes U.S. stablecoin issuer rules
items.summary: The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency finalized rules implementing the GENIUS Act, including uniform requirements for permitted stablecoin issuers and restrictions on stablecoin yield payments.[1][3]

items.title: SEC advances $132 million XRP-linked fundraising plan
items.summary: Evernorth filed to register up to 11.5 million shares tied to warrants that could raise approximately $132.2 million for XRP reserves. Ripple separately backed the SEC’s proposed digital-asset regulatory framework.[1][2]

items.title: Solana launches Alpenglow network overhaul
items.summary: Solana’s Alpenglow upgrade went live, replacing its voting system and targeting roughly 150-millisecond transaction finality after extensive testing.[5]

items.title: STRK gains more than 46% in 24 hours
items.summary: Starknet’s STRK token reached approximately $0.12 and was reported trading near $0.104, up 46.4% over 24 hours.[6]

items.title: Sui begins phased Hashi mainnet launch
items.summary: Sui announced that Hashi’s phased mainnet launch would begin during October, with more than $500 million in committed capital and Anchorage joining as a custody and liquidity partner.[9]

items.title: France advances 31% tax on crypto-to-stablecoin trades
items.summary: France’s National Assembly approved an amendment proposing a roughly 31% capital-gains tax on crypto-to-stablecoin transactions, subject to the broader legislative process.[5][7]

items.title: Argentina keeps crypto out of banking integration plans
items.summary: Argentina’s central bank said it would not pursue integration of cryptocurrencies and digital assets into banking and payment channels during the next two years, leaving existing restrictions on financial institutions in place.[6]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA brings Respawn and DICE together for an unannounced shooter
items.summary: Electronic Arts announced that Respawn and DICE will collaborate on a future shooter, while continuing development of new Battlefield projects and promising continued investment in Apex Legends. The company did not name the project, though reports have linked it to a possible Star Wars: Battlefront title.

items.title: EA confirms Fight Night revival and Project Gridiron
items.summary: EA Sports said Fight Night is in pre-production, marking the boxing series’ return after more than a decade. EA also revealed Project Gridiron, a social-first open-world American football game.

items.title: EA closes BioWare and cancels early Mass Effect development
items.summary: EA said it will close BioWare and its Edmonton workspace after ending early development on the next Mass Effect project. The company also said it will focus on fewer large-scale action-adventure games, including Marvel’s Iron Man and the next Star Wars Jedi.

items.title: EA pauses The Sims: Project Lotus
items.summary: Electronic Arts paused development on The Sims’ Project Lotus to prioritize Project Evergreen, which the company described as its main long-term focus for the franchise.

items.title: Crimson Desert DLC announced for October 29
items.summary: Pearl Abyss’ Crimson Desert is set to receive the Charting the Unknown DLC on October 29. Reported additions include marriage, castle ownership and business management features.

items.title: Video Game History Foundation adds more than 300 Japan game-industry photos
items.summary: The Video Game History Foundation added more than 300 previously unseen photographs documenting Japan’s late-1990s and early-2000s game scene to its free digital library.
items.source: VGC / Video Game History Foundation coverage

items.title: LoL patch 26.21 nerfs Jinx, Caitlyn and Lee Sin
items.summary: The latest League of Legends patch includes balance changes targeting Jinx, Caitlyn and Lee Sin, among other competitive updates.
